lessons.title: Missed It at Work? Claiming HRA While Filing Your ITR

body.text: Your employer's proof deadline is not the law's deadline. The HRA exemption is finally claimed in your income tax return. But the return has a deadline of its own, and for HRA it is stricter than most people realise: miss the original due date and you will usually lose the exemption for that year.

children.text: Thousands of salaried employees find in June that their salary TDS certificate shows no HRA exemption, even though they paid rent all year. Some missed the January proof window. Some joined late. Some had an employer that would not accept rent paid to a parent. The good news is that none of this is final. The bad news is that the fix has a deadline.
Why Your Form 130 and Your Return Can Differ
Form 130, which replaced Form 16, records what your employer allowed for TDS. Your return records what the law allows you. They can legitimately differ.

children.text: A salaried person with no business income can opt out of the default new regime under Section 202 only in a return filed by the due date under Section 263(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 139(1) of the 1961 Act). Since HRA exemption exists only in the old regime, the type of return you file decides whether you can claim it.

body.caption: Which return can carry an HRA claim

cells: Original return, Section 263(1)
Due date, generally 31 July 2027 for salaried individuals filing ITR-1 or ITR-2
Yes, by choosing the old regime in the return
Belated return, Section 263(4)
After the due date, generally up to 31 December 2027
Usually no. You cannot opt out of the new regime in a belated return, so HRA exemption is not available
Revised return, Section 263(5)
Up to 12 months from the end of the tax year, so 31 March 2028. A fee applies if revised after 9 months
To correct an HRA figure in a return that already chose the old regime on time, yes
Updated return, Section 263(6)
Up to 48 months, with additional tax
No. Updated returns are for reporting more income, not for claiming new exemptions or bigger refunds

body.label: The date that matters most for HRA
body.value: The original due date, usually 31 July
body.context: File by then and choose the old regime, and you can claim the exemption even if your employer allowed nothing. File late and the exemption is usually gone for that year.

body.text: The revised return window was extended by the Finance Act, 2026 to 12 months from the end of the tax year, with a fee of ₹1,000 (income up to ₹5 lakh) or ₹5,000 (above ₹5 lakh) for revisions filed after 9 months. Use it to fix a wrong HRA figure. Do not count on it to switch regimes after the due date, since the rules on changing the regime choice in a revised return are not clear-cut.

children.text: Worked Example: Claiming What Payroll Missed

Rohan works in Pune on a gross salary of ₹18,00,000, with basic ₹80,000 and HRA ₹40,000 a month. He pays ₹38,000 a month rent in Kothrud and has a home loan on a flat in Nashik where his parents live. He declared the old regime and submitted his home loan and 80C proofs, but missed the rent proof deadline. His Form 130 shows no HRA exemption.
His correct exempt HRA for tax year 2026-27, with Pune now a 50% city, is the smallest of ₹4,80,000, ₹4,56,000 minus ₹96,000 = ₹3,60,000, and ₹4,80,000: ₹3,60,000.

children.text: Rohan should also check the new regime: it would cost him ₹1,50,800, more than his old regime tax of ₹1,21,680. So claiming HRA in the old regime is the right choice, and he must do it in a return filed by the due date.
Filing the Claim, Step by Step

cells: 1. Pick the right form
ITR-1 or ITR-2 for most salaried individuals, as notified for the tax year
Use the form that matches all your income, not just salary
2. Opt out of the new regime
Select the old regime in the return
This is only possible in a return filed by the due date
3. Enter salary as per Form 130
Gross salary, then exempt allowances
Add together Form 130s from all employers in the year
4. Claim the HRA exemption
Enter it under allowances exempt from tax, with any rent and HRA details the form asks for
Calculate it yourself using the city of your rented home, not your office
5. Enter other deductions
Home loan interest, 80C, 80D and others under the old regime
Only claim what you can document
6. Check tax and refund
Compare with TDS in your Form 130 and AIS
A refund larger than expected usually means a mistake
7. E-verify
Verify the return, for example through Aadhaar OTP, within the permitted time
An unverified return is treated as not filed

body.text: In 2025, tax professionals pointed out that the ITR utility for assessment year 2025-26 asked for "place of work" when computing HRA, even though the law looks at where the rented home is. Whatever the utility prompts, work out your exemption using Rule 279 and the location of your home, and make sure the figure you report matches that calculation.

markDefs.definition: The provision of the Income-tax Act, 2025 under which returns are processed and an intimation of tax payable or refund due is issued. It replaced Section 143(1) of the 1961 Act.

children.text: of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 143(1) of the 1961 Act). Because your HRA claim will not match your Form 130, the system may flag it. You may receive a communication asking you to explain the difference, or proposing an adjustment. Respond on the e-filing portal with your rent agreement, receipts, bank statements and landlord PAN. A genuine, documented claim is usually accepted, and the refund follows.

body.title: Quick Check: Which Return Works?
body.question: Divya paid genuine rent all year but her employer allowed no HRA exemption. She wants the old regime. In which of these can she claim the exemption?
options: A belated return filed on 20 October
An updated return filed two years later
An original return filed on 25 July, before the due date
Only by asking her employer to reissue Form 130
body.explanation: An original return filed by the due date is where a salaried person can opt out of the new regime and claim HRA. A belated return cannot carry that choice, and an updated return cannot be used to claim a new exemption or a bigger refund. Her employer does not need to reissue Form 130.

body.title: Try It: Neha's Refund
body.prompt: Neha's employer allowed no HRA exemption, but she correctly claims ₹2,00,000 in her return filed by the due date under the old regime. Her taxable income stays within the 20% slab both before and after the exemption. What refund does the exemption create, including 4% cess? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: ₹2,00,000 × 20% = ₹40,000, plus 4% cess of ₹1,600, gives ₹41,600. That is tax her employer deducted as TDS that she did not owe.

body.title: Scenario: Filed in September
body.scenario: Karthik pays ₹35,000 a month rent in Chennai with full documents, but his employer allowed no HRA exemption because he never declared the old regime. He is busy in July and files his return on 12 September 2027, claiming the old regime and HRA exemption for tax year 2026-27.
body.prompt: What is likely to happen, and what should Karthik learn from it?
body.modelAnswer: Because 12 September is after the due date, his return is a belated return. A salaried person cannot opt out of the new regime in a belated return, so his return is likely to be processed under the new regime, and the HRA exemption and other old regime deductions will not be allowed. He may also owe a late filing fee and interest if any tax is unpaid. For many people the new regime is not much worse, but if the old regime would have saved him tax, that saving is lost for the year. The lesson: if you intend to use the old regime, treat the original due date as a hard deadline, and file on time even if everything else is not perfect. A wrong figure can be revised later. A missed deadline usually cannot be undone.

body.title: Claiming a Missed HRA Exemption
steps: Download Form 130 from each employer and your AIS from the e-filing portal
Recalculate your exempt HRA using actual rent, salary for HRA and the city of your rented home, period by period if anything changed
Compare old regime tax, with HRA and other deductions, against new regime tax
If the old regime wins, file your original return and choose the old regime before the due date
Enter the HRA exemption and any rent details the form asks for, then check the refund against your TDS
Keep your rent agreement, receipts, bank statements and landlord PAN ready to answer any communication

body.label: Income Tax e-filing portal
body.description: File and e-verify your return, download AIS, track your refund and respond to any communication about your HRA claim.

cards.definition: A return filed by the due date under Section 263(1). For salaried individuals, the only return in which you can opt out of the new regime.
A return filed after the due date under Section 263(4). The old regime option, and therefore HRA exemption, is usually not available.
A corrected return under Section 263(5), allowed up to 12 months from the end of the tax year, with a fee after 9 months.
A return under Section 263(6) to report additional income, with extra tax. It cannot be used to claim a new exemption or larger refund.
Processing of returns and issue of intimations under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Replaced Section 143(1).

points: Missing your employer's proof deadline does not cost you the HRA exemption. You can claim it in your return
You must choose the old regime in an original return filed by the due date, usually 31 July, to claim HRA
A belated return usually cannot carry the old regime choice, so the HRA exemption is lost for that year
Revised returns, now allowed up to 12 months from the end of the tax year, can fix a wrong HRA figure in a timely return
Updated returns cannot be used to claim a missed exemption or a bigger refund
Expect questions when your claim differs from Form 130, and answer them with your agreement, receipts, bank records and landlord PAN

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or financial advice. Due dates, return forms and processing rules can change each year. Provisions reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, as understood at the time of writing. Verify current rules on the e-filing portal or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
